subject: Biology
title: Pineal, Thymus, & Gonadal Endocrine Secretions
learningObjectives: Explain the role of Melatonin (Tryptophan derivative) in regulating 24-hr circadian rhythms
Describe Thymosins and the post-pubertal involution of the Thymus gland
Detail gonadal secretions: Leydig cell Testosterone, Sertoli cell Inhibin, Follicular Estrogen, and Corpus Luteum Progesterone
content:
### 8.1 The Pineal Gland

Located on the dorsal side of the forebrain (epithalamus). Secretes **Melatonin** (an amino acid derivative synthesized from **L-Tryptophan**).
- **Functions**: Regulates the 24-hour diurnal **Circadian Rhythm** (sleep-wake cycle), body temperature, skin pigmentation, menstrual cycles, and immune defense.
- **Light-Dark Regulation**: Photic input from retinal ganglion cells signals the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), suppressing melatonin secretion during daytime light and promoting secretion during darkness.

### 8.2 The Thymus Gland

A lobular organ situated between the lungs behind the sternum on the dorsal side of the aorta. Secretes peptide hormones called **Thymosins**.
- **Functions**: Essential for the maturation and differentiation of **T-Lymphocytes** (mediating **Cell-Mediated Immunity**) and promoting antibody production by plasma cells.
- **Involution**: The thymus is prominent at birth and enlarges through childhood, but undergoes progressive **Involution (atrophy)** after puberty, largely replaced by adipose tissue in the elderly.

### 8.3 Gonadal Endocrine Secretions

- **Testes (Interstitial / Leydig Cells)**: Luteinizing Hormone (LH) stimulates Leydig cells to produce **Androgens (Testosterone)**, driving male secondary sexual characteristics, male libido, and supporting Spermatogenesis. Sertoli cells secrete **Inhibin** to selectively down-regulate anterior pituitary FSH release.
- **Ovaries**:
  - **Ovarian Follicles**: Secrete **Estrogens (Estradiol)** under FSH stimulation, driving female secondary sexual characteristics and endometrial proliferation.
  - **Corpus Luteum**: Formed from the ruptured Graafian follicle post-ovulation under LH influence; secretes **Progesterone** ("Pregnancy Hormone"), which prepares and maintains the uterine endometrium for implantation and stimulates mammary alveoli. Also secretes **Relaxin**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Suprachiasmatic Master Clock & Melatonin
conceptBreakdown.explanation: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of the anterior hypothalamus acts as the central circadian pacemaker, regulating nocturnal pineal melatonin synthesis via sympathetic postganglionic projections from the superior cervical ganglion.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Dual Origin of Relaxin
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Relaxin is secreted by the corpus luteum and placenta during late gestation, softening the pubic symphysis fibrocartilage and dilating the cervix to facilitate parturition.
